title: Detect Capital
summary: Determine if the capital usage in a word is correct based on the rules: all letters are capitals, all letters are not capitals, or only the first letter is capital.
statement: Determine if the capital usage in a word is correct based on the rules: all letters are capitals, all letters are not capitals, or only the first letter is capital.
constraints: 1 <= len(word) <= 100; only uppercase and lowercase English letters.
Accept exactly three patterns: every letter uppercase, every letter lowercase, or only the first letter uppercase.
hints: These are three patterns of case, not three special words.
Count uppercase letters, then consider where a sole uppercase letter occurs.
Accept count=0, count=length, or count=1 with an uppercase first character.
A one-letter word satisfies an all-one-case rule. A lowercase first letter followed by a capital is never title case.
editorial: The number of capitals identifies all-lowercase and all-uppercase words. The only remaining accepted count is one, and that capital must be first. This classification is exhaustive and uses constant extra space. The independent oracle matches the three literal case-pattern languages with a regular expression.

tests.explanation: All three letters are uppercase, so return true; capitals are not limited to the first position.
Return false: uppercase F followed by lowercase letters and another uppercase G matches none of the three allowed patterns.
